claim_en: The two-verse grid: מכה איש ('one who strikes a man') and Lev 24's ואיש כי יכה ('a man who strikes') each close the gap the other leaves — woman and minor VICTIMS included, non-viable births (nefalim) excluded (victim must be bar kayama, fit to live); woman STRIKER liable, minor striker excluded by verse.
source: TT 21:12 (B1); MRS (B2); Chafetz Chaim on Sifra (B3); Malbim ish/adam grid (B20); Riva + Siftei Chakhamim (B32)

claim_en: Causation totality: ומת ('and he dies') = liable only if THIS blow took the WHOLE soul — ten men with ten sticks all exempt (Sanhedrin 78a); but he who finishes an already-beaten victim (בלבלו 'finished him') is liable: the causation cut lands on the final blow.
source: TT 21:12:3 (B1); MRS 21:12 (B2); Malbim vs R. Yehudah b. Beteira (B20)

claim_en: The two-courts architecture: the doubled מות יומת ('he shall surely be put to death') = ALL death-deserving stand in Heaven's docket and God delegated a SUBSET to earthly courts; the ger toshav (resident alien) victim exits the delegated subset — רעהו ('his fellow') exclusion, 'exempt before courts of flesh and blood, their judgment handed to Heaven' — while the slave victim stays inside it.
source: Or HaChaim (B25, marquee); Yalkut 325 Asi b. Akiva — tannaitic (B34); MT Rotzeach 2:11 + Kessef Mishneh (B6/B7); Gur Aryeh minor-fetus asymmetry (B17)

claim_en: Execution modes: the murderer dies by SWORD (נקם ינקם 'avenged be avenged' ↔ חרב נקמת 'avenging sword', locked by the eglah-arufah (broken-necked heifer) beheading hekesh and the freeman kal-vachomer); every UNMARKED מות יומת defaults to chenek (strangulation — the lightest, by the leniency-default rule); severity order stoning > burning > sword > chenek; ואהבת לרעך כמוך ('love your fellow as yourself') compiled into procedure: 'choose him a beautiful death'.
source: TT 21:15 (B1); MT Sanhedrin 14 (B6); JT Sanhedrin 7:1 (B6); TYT Sanhedrin 9:1 (B4); Maskil LeDavid (B22); MRS (B2)

claim_en: Kim leih bederabbah mineih (the one-penalty absorption family): derived at the BLOCK SEAM — אין כסף ('no money', 21:11) juxtaposed to מכה איש ומת = 'no money: he dies' (one does not die AND pay); משום רשעה אחת ('for ONE wickedness you charge him'); one ACT carrying death and payment → death only, SEQUENTIAL acts → both; extended to Heaven's docket via the ason-weld (Gen 42:38): karet-class liability also cancels co-liable payment, and per Tanna d'vei Chizkiyah even without warning (Rambam rules so); lashes-vs-payment: pay, don't flog (Ulla) — the Yom-Kippur injurer the lone explicit exception (רק שבתו יתן 'only his idleness he shall give' — a ribui, an expander).
source: Lekach Tov 21:12:1 (B9) + Tur HaArokh 21:12 (B12) — dual seam attestation; TT 21:22 (B1); MRS simultaneity rule (B2); Ketubot 30a-38a engine (B5); Peri Megadim/TD"Ch (B28); MT Chovel 4:9 (B7)

claim_en: Refuge is calibrated to the PURE-ACCIDENT band only: karov le-mezid (near-willful — meant to throw two cubits, threw four) is excluded ABOVE (no refuge, and the blood-avenger who kills him goes free; the transferred-intent killer likewise exempt from death AND exile); karov le-ones (near-duress) is excluded BELOW (needs no atonement); the Makkot 7b word-battery assigns one exclusion gate per word of the verse.
source: TT 21:13 (B1); Makkot 7b battery (B5); Mizrachi (B24); Hirsch guilt-window (B30); Bartenura three-grades (B15)

claim_en: והאלהים אנה לידו ('and God caused it to meet his hand') = the divine scheduler: two unwitnessed killers — one willful, one accidental — are appointed to one inn; the willful dies under the ladder, the accidental exiles (Reish Lakish, Makkot 10b). The verse's two clauses = the two shegagah grades chained by the inn-mechanism (GRA ms); the scheduler does sentencing algebra (the harsher sudden death equalized by the missing anticipatory anguish); God supplies the CAUSE, not the event.
source: TT 21:13:2 (B1); Rashi + Gen 9:5 crossref (B9); HaKtav VeHaKabbalah/GRA ms (B18); Divrei David (B8); Maskil LeDavid + Paaneach Raza mechanisms (B22/B25); Od Yosef Chai cave-parable (B24); Alshekh (B14)

claim_en: ושמתי לך מקום ('I will appoint you a PLACE'): the wilderness refuge = the LEVITE CAMP; and the makom↔makom chain (Issi ben Akiva) welds refuge's 'place' to אל יצא איש ממקומו ('let no man go out of his place', the manna verse) → the 2,000-cubit Shabbat limit (techum) is measured off the refuge verse — deployed as practical eruv law down to the Siddur.
source: MRY Nezikin 4:16 (B3); Eruvin 51a (B17); JT Eruvin 4:1 (B6); Malbim (B20); LT Deut 4:45 + Siddur Rashi 461 (B9); Kitzur BhT gematria seal (B12)

claim_en: Exile is ATONEMENT, not mere shelter — proven from the avenger-less slave victim (no kin → no avenger, yet his inadvertent killer is exiled) and from bones carried to the refuge city after death; ONE exile atones many shogeg-killings; the term is deliberately UNFIXED (until the high priest dies) because it is a divinely-indexed variable sentence paying each shegagah's grade — refuse the hint and Heaven schedules a second killing, doubling the term.
source: Ohr Sameach Rotzeach 6:12 (B7); Sforno Num 35:25 (B12) + Or HaChaim (B25) — dual attestation; Hadar Zekenim (B19); Pardes Yosef proofs (B26)

claim_en: Hatraah (formal warning) is derived from the IMPERFECT aspect of וכי יזד ('if he schemes', ongoing): 'they warned him and he is STILL willful'; the warning must name WHICH death; בערמה ('with guile') excludes those without guile-capacity (deaf-mute, insane, minor) AND the authority contexts — erring physician, court flogger, father/teacher disciplining — exempt from death (Tosefta: liable to exile).
source: TT 21:14:1,3 (B1); Sifrei Zuta exemption list (B3); Riva mnin-lehatra'ah (B32); Ralbag (B29); Malbim schemer-vs-intender (B20)

claim_en: מעם מזבחי תקחנו למות ('from beside My altar you shall take him to die') — the altar as a JURISDICTIONAL FILTER: taken only 'to die' (money, lashes, exile are sheltered); מעם not מעל — the priest mid-service finishes, the not-yet-started is taken; only the Temple's altar, only its roof, only a priest with service in hand (Joab's errors); STANDING MACHLOKET at the crown interface: the GRA — the altar shields FROM crown-law until beit-din convicts (why Joab fled; why Solomon re-tried him in court terms) — vs the Netziv — the stealth-killer pericope is itself crown-law and the altar does not shield even from the KING.
source: TT 21:14:4 (B1); MRS (B2); MT Rotzeach 5:12 (B6); GRA Aderet Eliyahu (B14) + ms (B18); Netziv (B19); Malbim Yoav file (B20); Abarbanel contra-nations essay (B14)

claim_en: The jurisdictional clock: capital courts run only while the Temple stands AND the Sanhedrin sits in its chamber beside the altar ('forty years before the destruction capital cases ceased — the Sanhedrin was EXILED from its seat'); and the execution CALENDAR: execution overrides Temple service but NOT Shabbat, no capital trial on Friday (the verdict would sink); PIKUACH NEFESH (life-saving overrides Shabbat) is itself derived from our clause by R. Shimon b. Menasya's kal-vachomer.
source: MRS 40-years stamp (B2); TT (B1); MT Sanhedrin 14 (B6); Sanhedrin 35b + JT 4:6 (B5/B6); Amrot Hashem clock (B26); Yalkut 326 (B34); Sefer HaMitzvot intro (B7)

claim_en: The parent-striker is capital only WITH a wound (chaburah — even a drop of congealed blood counts), only while the parent LIVES (the curse differs on both counts); father alone OR mother alone suffices — ומכה אביו ואמו is the Torah's own paradigm of vav-as-OR (cited across the whole system: Jephthah's vow, Neh 6:12, גנבתי לילה 'stolen by night' — Gen 31:39).
source: TT 21:15 (B1); MRS quantified chaburah (B2); Sifra Emor (B3); Tur YD 241 (B13); IE grammar export (B10/B11); Radak Judges 11:31 (B12); Gra (B22)

claim_en: The rov/chazakah legal epistemology is ANCHORED here: the father-striker is executed though paternity rests on 'most intercourse follows the husband' (Chullin 11b), the murderer though the victim might have been a tereifah — courts execute on presumptions; the Chatam Sofer closes the scheming defense with the altar's own wordplay (מעם מזבחי — 'LEARN from My altar': the korbanot themselves run on rov against the tereifah ('fatally-stricken') doubt).
source: TT 21:15:1 (B1); Chullin 11b at source + Chatam Sofer (B16); JT Kiddushin 4:10 (B4); Chida (B24); Pardes Yosef two-minorities refinement (B26)

claim_en: Status-flags on the PARENT gate the child's liability: the wicked parent ('one who does not act as your people') — forbidden but exempt-if-done; REPENTANCE flips liability back on, even as the father walks to execution; honor is waivable but blow and curse are not, and once warning is accepted before witnesses the parent can no longer waive (the waiver-lock); pre-authorization ('strike me') removes the lav entirely; the healing carve — a son may bloodlet his father but should prefer another physician.
source: MT Mamrim 5:12 (B6); Tur YD 241 (B13); Paaneach Raza waiver-lock (B27) + Chida (B24); Minchat Chinukh pre-authorization (B27); TT healing (B1)

claim_en: The kidnap pipeline — liability requires ALL elements: steal + bring into his domain + USE (והתעמר בו, even under a perutah — leaning on the sleeping victim counts) + sell WHOLE (not half), with witnesses on the THEFT and witnesses on the SALE; ונמצא בידו ('and he is found in his hand') excludes the matzuy (regularly-present: father, schoolteacher, orphans' guardian); sold-to-relatives exempt until 'removed from his brothers'; and person-theft admits no owner-despair (yeush) — a human cannot be given up, the liability never lapses.
source: TT 21:16 (B1); MRS (B2); MT Theft 9:2,9:5 (B7); Malbim four-teachings (B20); BK 68b R. Yochanan (B5); Sanhedrin 11:1 (B3)

claim_en: The azharah/onesh split: 21:16 gives kidnap's PUNISHMENT, but the Torah never punishes without a separate WARNING verse — the Decalogue's לא תגנב ('you shall not steal') IS the kidnap warning, read capital by its neighbors (davar ha-lamed me-inyano), while property-theft's warning is Lev 19:11's plural; declaration (Decalogue) and enforcement (Mishpatim) are separate required statements.
source: MRY Bachodesh 8:12 (B3); LT Exod 20:13 (B9); Rashbam penalty-appendix (B30); Malbim (B20); Pesikta Rabbati 21 chizzuk-grid (B28); Yalkut 298/322 (B34)

claim_en: Verse ORDER is legal data — Rashi says so in his own words (the kidnap-verse 'interrupting' the parent-laws encodes the strike↔curse hekesh dispute: ונראה לי היינו פלוגתא); SIX placement theories stand on record, the causal-biography multi-attested (the stolen child grows up not knowing his parents and comes to strike and curse them — 'the sin is on the kidnapper's head'); the pericope as a לא זו אף זו ladder — contact strictly decreasing (kill → wound → no blow → word alone), liability held at death, with Gur Aryeh's dignity-rationale.
source: Rashi 21:16:3 (B9, marquee); Saadia/IE (B10); Ramban (B11); Tur (B12); Chizkuni + Bekhor Shor ladder (B12/B13); Radbaz 2:295 (B27); Bamidbar Rabbah 9:7 (B15); Gur Aryeh (B17); Riva (B32)

claim_en: The Joseph sale RUN AGAINST the statute's element list: the brothers exempt because title-possession/use fails — Joseph was sold FROM THE PIT and the buyers pulled him out (ונמצא בידו and והתעמר בו both unmet); the tradition then reads the Ten Martyrs as the verse's trans-generational enforcement (מות יומת as the second death), with Benjamin's goblet ('found in his hand') replaying the element.
source: Ben Yehoyada Kiddushin 81b (B4); Abarbanel placement theory (B14); Megalleh Amukkot network (B22/B23); Bahya Ten-Martyrs (B13); Bereshit Rabbati pre-Sinai liability (B16)

claim_en: The curser: liable even AFTER the parent's death (vs the striker, exempt — a wound needs flesh; the curse wounds the soul, which lives); the curse must carry the NAME; death = STONING via דמיו בו ('his blood is on him', from the ov/yidoni necromancers); mere verbal disgrace = rabbinic lashes; and the words-over-deeds doctrine stands on our 21:15/17 pair — 'the Torah is stricter on words than deeds' (striker strangled, curser stoned), because the curse bears the Name, reaches past death and out of presence.
source: TT 21:17 (B1); MRS חומר בדיבור (B2); Sanhedrin 11:1 (B3); Tosefta Arakhin 2:6 (B4); Midrash Tannaim (B10); Sefer Chasidim + Paaneach Raza rationales (B27); Pesikta Rabbati 23 three-partners (B29)

claim_en: The assessment doctrine (omed): באבן או באגרוף ('with stone or with fist') = the two POLES of assessment — stone = instrument-lethality, fist = spot-lethality — and the instrument must be death-capable AND witness-assessable: produced in court; a stone lost before witnesses saw it exits the capital track (for damages the victim swears and collects); iron has NO size threshold ('even a needle kills').
source: TT R. Natan hekesh (B1); MT Chovel 1:18 (B7); LT 21:18:2 (B9); SA CM 420:28 (B32); Malbim two-poles (B21); Sifrei Bamidbar 160 iron (B3); Tzafnat Paneach three assessment-types (B33)

claim_en: The custody doctrine: assessed-for-death → the striker is JAILED until the victim's outcome is known (chovshin oto — 'would you think this one walks in the market and that one is executed?'); ונקה המכה ('the striker is cleared') = released from prison; והתהלך בחוץ על משענתו ('walks outside on his support') = on HIS OWN restored health (Onkelos על בוריה — the de-literalized staff, one of R. Yishmael's three canonical mashal-readings).
source: TT 21:19 (B1); Rashi חובשים (B9); IE prison (B11); Onkelos (B8); MT Rotzeach 4:4 (B7); Sifrei Devarim 237 whitelist (B3); Malbim (B21); Hirsch (B30)

claim_en: The assessment STATE MACHINE (typed verdicts with transitions): assessed-for-death → death-track, money extinguished; assessed-for-money → money-track, death extinguished; assessed-death-then-improved → SECOND assessment for money, payment retroactive FROM THE BLOW; assessed-to-live-then-died → striker exempt from death, pays the five heads to the HEIRS; improved-then-worsened-then-died → the sages (died of the first blow → liable) vs R. Nechemiah (the walking acquitted him); יעמד read as a COURT verb — assessed to stand a day = acquitted even if he later dies.
source: Tosefta BK 9:2 (B4, the machine verbatim); Sanhedrin 78b (B6); TYT Nazir 9:4 (B4); JT Sanhedrin 9:3 chiddush-vs-error theories (B6); Meshekh Chokhmah יעמד (B23); Or HaChaim heirs-payment (B25)

claim_en: THE FIVE HEADS as a struct with per-field formulas and per-field nullability: nezek = market worth before minus after (slave-valuation); tzaar = what one would pay to have it done by drug instead of knife — pain owed even ATOP damage, compensable at ZERO damage (spit-burn on the nail, stones loaded, snow poured), and SUBJECTIVE ('if he was soft and delicate his pain is doubled'); shevet = idle cucumber-watchman wage (because the hand-price was already paid under nezek — an explicit anti-double-count rule); rippui = projected costs with the relapse ladder; boshet = indexed by the shamer and the shamed (Deut 25:11) — 'no limb lost → no nezek head; no pain → no tzaar head': each head independently zeroed.
source: MRS Ben Azzai class-proof + struct (B2); Mishnah BK 8:1 (B3); MRY 8:23 (B3); SMaG Pos 70 deployed code (B7); Tur CM 420 (B12); Yalkut 337-339 (B34/B35); Ralbag shoresh 18 (B29)

claim_en: Per-head MENS-REA gates on one damage event: אדם מועד לעולם ('man is forever forewarned') — nezek is strict liability, owed awake or asleep, accidental, coerced (derived from the wound-verse's redundancy against Lev 24:19); shevet+rippui are written inside the quarrel-verse → mezid-context binds them; boshet alone requires INTENT (ושלחה ידה 'she reached out her hand'); the shogeg who blinds pays nezek only — and the same physics is evaluated by five different intent thresholds across domains (damages / four heads / Shabbat / exile / slave-exit: BK 26b's cross-domain ladder).
source: TT 21:25 (B2); TYT BK 2:6 per-head table (B4); BK 26b ladder (B5); Hirsch intent-gradient (B30); JT Ketubot 3:3 symmetric rule (B5)

claim_en: The healing cluster: רק שבתו יתן ורפא ירפא ('only his idleness he shall give, and heal he shall heal') — the SPLIT phrasing = EARMARKED damages (the fee goes to the physicians; the victim cannot pocket it, the striker cannot say 'I will heal you myself' — 'you are to me a lurking lion' — nor offer a free doctor: 'a physician who heals for nothing is worth nothing'); the doubled verb = relapse re-liability (from the original wound → liable again, even four or five rounds) AND the PHYSICIAN'S LICENSE ('shall the doctor say: God smote and I heal?') — codified to SA YD 336:1 (license, mitzvah, within pikuach nefesh; erred with court-license → exempt below, liable in Heaven's court; killed and knows it → exile); רק exempts the self-aggravating victim (honey against orders); counter-pole on record: Ibn Ezra scopes the license to man-inflicted external wounds only.
source: TT (B1); LT license marquee (B9); Ramban earmark marquee (B11); Tur CM 420 negotiation protocol (B12); Malbim piel-grammar (B21); Torat HaAdam judge-model (B33); SA YD 336 (B32); IE anti-medicine essay (B10/B11); Bahya/Kitzur BhT dagesh-law (B12/B13/B32)

claim_en: The day-or-two safe-harbor is a TWO-KEY gate: כספו ('his money' = exclusive title) AND תחתיו ('under him' = current subjection) — the seller who reserved 30 days' service, the buyer, partnership slaves, and the half-slave ALL fail (executed like any killer; the four-way tannaitic fork on the 30-day sale litigates whether usufruct counts as ownership INSIDE a capital exemption clause); struck-then-SOLD-then-died → exempt ('his blow and his death must both be in his ownership'); and the window itself = 24 hours מעת לעת ('a day that is like two days' — Targum Jonathan (the Aramaic rendering) writes it into the verse verbatim).
source: MT Rotzeach 2:12-16 (B7, marquee); TT (B1); MRS 30-day case (B2); Tosefta BK 9:8 (B4); BK 90a/BB 50a-b fourfold (B5); TJ verbatim (B8); Malbim computation (B21); Hirsch two-reckonings (B31)

claim_en: ROD-ONLY: the safe-harbor applies solely to disciplinary instruments (rod, strap — בשבט ('with a rod') licenses discipline, never execution-grade force); knife/sword/stone/fist assessed-lethal → executed even if death comes a year later (Rambam's own יראה לי, 2:14 — proven by the Tzafnat Paneach from the Mechilta's ox: the ox that killed a slave dies even after the day, so the owner's exemption must be instrument-gated); Kli Yakar's reverse-presumption: כי כספו הוא ('for he is his money') — no man destroys his own money, so the rod-blow is presumed non-mortal and a day-three death attributes to a new cause.
source: MT Rotzeach 2:14 (B7); TT (B1); Rashbam peshat ('rod = rebuke, sword = murder-mode') (B30); Or HaChaim intent-evidence (B25); Tzafnat Paneach (B27); Kli Yakar (B20); Netziv chronobiology (B19)

claim_en: נקם ינקם ('avenged shall be avenged') = death by SWORD (חרב נקמת, Lev 26:25); scoped to the CANAANITE slave only — the Gra's class-rule: wherever עבד ואמה ('slave and maidservant') are JUXTAPOSED the Canaanite is meant, because a Hebrew pair is demographically impossible (the amah exits at puberty, a male Hebrew slave cannot be a minor); and the vengeance-WORD is the point: the slave has no kin, so the COMMUNITY OF ISRAEL is his blood-avenger — 'the slave is their brother'; Onkelos renders אתדנא יתדן ('he shall surely be JUDGED') — vengeance as judicial process, root קם = standing-in-place (substitution, not rage).
source: TT (B1); MRS (B2); Gra class-rule (B19 ms/B27); Malbim vengeance-heat (B21); Hirsch community-goel marquee (B31); HaKtav VeHaKabbalah נקם word-study (B18); Ohr Sameach (B7)

claim_en: The transferred-intent fork is a LIVE tannaitic machloket carried in the block's own words: the sages/R. Elazar — meant-one-killed-another LIABLE (the brawl verse read as intended killing; real execution), vs Rebbi/R. Shimon/MRS — exempt (נפש תחת נפש = money via netinah↔netinah); the Sanhedrin 9:2 FORCE-VECTOR MATRIX evaluates sufficiency on the INTENDED vector (meant the loins with heart-sufficient force that landed on the heart → exempt; sufficient-for-intended force landing on an equally vulnerable other spot → liable); and the two brawl-words are a formal TRANSFER OPERATOR ('matzut IS merivah'): the payment heads named in each verse-family apply to both.
source: TT 21:22 R. Elazar (B1); MRS transfer operator + exempt-line (B2); Mishnah Sanhedrin 9:2 (B3); LT both voices (B9); Malbim (B21); Rebbi netinah chain (B6)

claim_en: The fetus is NOT a nefesh until birth — עובר ירך אמו (the fetus is its mother's limb): no execution for a fetus (its warning is doubt-warning — viability unproven until it 'exits to the world's air'), the hard-labor rule (dismember to save the mother UNTIL the head emerges), the condemned pregnant woman NOT reprieved for birth ('it is HER body'); the fetus-VALUE (with the pregnancy premium) belongs to the husband-at-CONCEPTION — divorced-and-remarried chains, illicit unions ('husband' even from zenut), all route to him; no husband-line → SHE keeps it; the Noahide differs on his own verse (liable for fetuses — 'blood of man IN man').
source: TT (B1); Tosefta BK 9:7 conception-timestamp (B4); Arakhin 7a + Bartenura (B4/B3); BK 42a-43a (B5); Divrei David fetus-status (B9); Gur Aryeh category-boundary (B17); Mizrachi/Maskil safek-warning chain (B22/B24); Malbim Noahide (B21)

claim_en: ענוש יענש ('punished he shall be punished') = MONEY (gezerah shavah from Deut 22:19's hundred-silver fine), CAPPED by ונתן בפלילים ('he shall give by the JUDGES' — pelilim = judges, proven from Deut 32:31 and 1 Sam 2:25); the husband must CLAIM (no suit → no collection) but the AMOUNT is the court's; Onkelos's grammatical NUMBER carries the classification — ישוי singular at 21:22 (husband claims; pure money) vs ישוון plural at 21:30 (judges impose unclaimed; kofer = atonement): kenas-vs-kaparah (fine-vs-atonement) read off one letter.
source: TT 21:22:9-14 (B2); Minei Targuma number-split (B8); GRA claim-vs-amount (B14); Netinah LaGer court-collection (B24); Ramban kenas-theory (B11); Rasag/Ezra 7:26 (B32)

claim_en: עין תחת עין ('eye for eye') = MONEY — the proof-TOURNAMENT preserved with live rebuttals: Chizkiyah's overshoot-impossibility ('eye for eye, not eye-AND-LIFE for eye' — literal blinding can kill), Rav Ashi's תחת↔תחת gezerah shavah, the pain/healing differentials that leak money at every margin, the Saadia–Ben Zuta debate (incommensurability; the poor-striker question met by the BLIND-BLINDER checkmate: the poor may grow rich, a blind man can never repay an eye), Ralbag's six-argument battery, Sforno's epistemic-precision safeguard (חסרון השערתנו — 'the deficit of our estimation'); Rambam: the money-reading has the standing of halakhah le-Moshe mi-Sinai, the verses asmakhta; and the TYPE BOUNDARY: נפש is literal but עין is money because Num 35:31 bars ransom for a murderer's LIFE — 'but you DO take ransom for limbs': the ransom-exclusion verse separates the two clauses.
source: TT 21:23-24 (B2); BK 83b-84a (B5); IE long recension (B11); Ralbag (B29); Sforno (B12); Bahya/RC three proofs (B13); Malbim (B21); Hirsch tachat word-study (B31); Em LaMikra ideal-measure (B17)

claim_en: The tachat/bet PREPOSITION SYSTEM: our נפש תחת נפש ('life in place of life' — tachat = the ANTECEDENT cause) vs the plotting witnesses' נפש בנפש (bet = the cause YET TO COME) — the Sadducees refuted by preposition (the victim must still stand); Ben Azzai's class-proof: חבורה appears in both verse-families → the whole תחת-series is PAYMENT, except nefesh (excluded by the no-ransom verse); and Onkelos's SADDUCEE-FILTER law: the Targum deviates into the received halakhah exactly where the Sadducees disputed the Sages (חלף 'in exchange for' throughout the list) and stays literal where they conceded (נפשא חלף נפשא) — pseudo-Jonathan's inserted דמי ('the VALUE of') marks the other channel; Tafsir Rasag writes the indemnity into the verse itself: ודית עין בדל עין ('the DIYA of an eye in place of an eye').
source: HaKtav VeHaKabbalah Deut 19:19 marquee (B18) + Hirsch Deut 19:21 (B30); MRS Ben Azzai (B2); Makkot 1:6 (B3); Netinah LaGer filter-law marquee (B24); Tafsir Rasag (B33); HaKtav indemnity-table re-parse (B19)

claim_en: The liability-vs-execution split (the compromise the tradition itself preserves): Ibn Ezra — liability is LITERAL, execution MONETARY (the eye is forfeit unless ransomed — עינו תחת עינו אם לא יתן כפרו), modeled on the goring ox's יומת→כופר pair; Em LaMikra quotes the TWELVE TABLES verbatim ('si membrum rupit, ni cum eo pacit, talio esto' — Roman talion WITH the ransom-option) as the structural parallel, and reads eye-for-eye as the IDEAL MEASURE retained in the text, which courts must approximate and never exceed; 'as we received the Written so we received the Oral — no difference' (IE's rule at the debate).
source: IE Katzar + long recension (B10/B11); Em LaMikra (B17, marquee); Abarbanel/Kuzari (B22); Beit Yosef CM 425 paradigm-of-non-literal (B15); Recanati seventy-faces (B33)

claim_en: The limb-tip exit predicate (klal-uferat-uklal — 'general, particular, general' — on tooth+eye): everything LIKE the particulars — EXPOSED and NON-REGENERATING — frees: the 24 rashei evarim (limb-ends); milk-tooth excluded (regrows), castration/tongue fail exposed; a physical ACT ON the organ is required (shouted beside his ear → not freed: flight was possible) but the damage may be internal (skull-blow whose fluid blinded → freed); INTENT AT THE ORGAN even benevolent — the master-dentist who meant to scale and knocked out the tooth frees him (שיחק באדון 'he outplayed the master'); destruction must be real and irreversible (dimmed sight, removable cataract-film → not freed) — care owed slaves must EXCEED care owed free men.
source: TT 21:26-27 (B2); MRS intent-gate (B3); Bavli Kiddushin 24a-b live derivation (B4); MT Slaves 5:4-11 (B7); Tosefta BK 9:9 causal-chains (B4); Malbim (B21); Hirsch dentist + knas (B31)

claim_en: The exit is a KENAS (fine): the award is FLAT (eye = tooth) and far exceeds the damage → preventive punishment, so fines-law governs — it attaches only through COURT AND WITNESSES, self-admission defeats it (R. Gamliel came rejoicing to free Tabi and R. Yehoshua blocked it: modeh bi-knas patur), and AGENCY shields the master (ordered another to maim → NOT freed, as agency shielded the sender from the sword: 'the striker dies, not the sender').
source: Mishnah Shevuot 5:5 + Tosefta BK 9:9 (B4); JT Ketubot 3:10 + BK 74b Tabi story (B5); Sifrei Zuta agency rule (B3); GRA kenas (B14); Hirsch (B31); Tzafnat Paneach payment-vs-fine nafka minot (B33)

claim_en: The SELF-PAYMENT LOOP is the statute's design rationale: a master fined for maiming his own slave would pay HIMSELF (what a slave acquires his master acquires — damages are useless to the slave, 'his only remedy is FREEDOM'), so the Torah converts the eye-money into his RANSOM from his master's hand and escalates to emancipation — the stringency riding on לעולם בהם תעבדו ('forever you shall work them'), the class the exit carves.
source: Ralbag closing rationale (B29, before Malbim); Malbim 21:26:1 marquee (B21); Chizkuni remedy-design (B12); Sefer HaMitzvot Pos 235 (B7); MRY 9:1 class-exit (B3)

claim_en: The Ham aetiology as LEGAL cause, fourth-attested and stated by the compilation in its own voice: slavery ENTERED the world through Ham's EYE and MOUTH ('and Ham SAW... and TOLD' — bared/gnashed his teeth) and was cursed with bondage — so it EXITS through eye and tooth: 'when the sinning limbs are struck, the body exits the punishment of slavery' — manumission as measure-for-measure UNDOING of the first slavery-curse; eschatological binding: God holds HIMSELF to 21:26 ('I struck both their eyes — is it not the law that they go free?' — the manumission of Jerusalem), and the suffering blind student is 'free for the World to Come'.
source: LT 21:27:2 + Tanchuma Noach (B10); R. Bahya (B13/B28); Rosh curse-organs closure (B32); Yalkut 339:5 own-voice + 850:5 (B35); Pesikta Rabbati 8 (B28); BR 92:1 (B16); Alshekh k"v crown (B15)

claim_en: Exit composition and bounds: eye then tooth IN SEQUENCE → freed on the first AND PAID for the second like any injured freeman (both-at-once → freedom only, per the tosefta line); the WRIT machloket — R. Shimon: a get shichrur is required (shiluach↔shiluach from divorce) vs R. Meir: free from the moment of the blow (לחפשי ישלחנו word-order proof); the HEBREW slave never exits by tooth/eye (לא תצא כצאת העבדים); split-title slaves (melog/tzon-barzel) are outside BOTH the day-window and the exit (split title fails כספו in both directions); and the emancipation does not propagate into the womb — fetuses do not exit by their mother's tooth-and-eye.
source: TT (B2); Bavli Kiddushin 24 (B4); JT Gittin 4:4 + JT BK 5:5 (B5); JT Yevamot 7:1 dual-ownership table (B4); Rashi Hebrew-fence (B9); Malbim (B21); Or HaChaim two-triggers (B25)

claim_en: אין עונשין מן הדין ('we do not punish from inference') — NO PUNISHMENT FROM INFERENCE: penal liability must rest on explicit text, never on derived logic ('the a-fortiori was available, the verse troubled itself to write it anyway' — derivable ≠ enforceable); the rule guards THIRD parties (the rodef-inversion: a k"v leniency to the master would have turned the slave's RESCUER into a murderer); yet k"v may still SPECIFY a written-but-underspecified law (gilui milta) — how בשבט gets its lethal-capacity spec and the murderer's sword survives.
source: MRY 7:7,7:9 (B3); Sifrei Bamidbar 160 (B3); TYT Sanhedrin 5:1 (B4); Divrei David gilui-milta boundary (B9); Da'at Zekenim + Hadar Zekenim rodef-inversion (B17/B19); Kenesset HaGedolah (B27)

claim_en: The CLASS-EXIT operator (yatza mi-klalo, 'it exited its class') runs three ways in this one block, each parshah justified by the delta it encodes: the parent-striker exits the payment class to be STRICTER (death); the slave-death exits the homicide class to be MORE LENIENT (the day-window); the slave-maiming exits Lev 25:46's work-them-forever class to be stricter ON THE MASTER (emancipation); and the davar-chadash rule bounds it: a TOTAL exit never back-propagates onto its class (no free-man day-window ever — the sword locked from both sides), while כי כספו הוא is the RETURN-clause restoring the slave to the class after 24 hours.
source: MRY 5:1/7:1/9:1 (B3); Divrei David davar-chadash (B8); Bartenura both-sides lock (B15); Maskil LeDavid exit-mechanics (B22); Mizrachi return-clause (B24); Levush HaOrah dialectic (B20)

claim_en: THE TWO-TABLETS ARCHITECTURE: Mishpatim is the Decalogue's ENFORCEMENT LAYER, tablet by tablet — the slave-laws answered the FIRST word of the first tablet ('out of the house of slaves'), מכה איש answers the first word of the second (לא תרצח — the Decalogue warned but did not punish; Mishpatim supplies the penalty), and לא תגנב = kidnap enforced at 21:16; attested in peshat (Rashbam: the block = the Decalogue's penalty-appendix), in the halakhic midrash (the azharah/onesh split), and in the Pesikta's own voice (each gentle Sinai word backed by a hard enforcement verse).
source: R. Bahya 21:12 (B13, marquee); Rashbam (B30); MRY Bachodesh 8:12 (B3); Pesikta Rabbati 21 (B28); Ramban civilization-floor (B11)
